$schema_note: rna-figure design tokens -- the RNA figure house standard for the Chanfreau and Sumner spaces. SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for both colour layers, typography, geometry and the two floors. Every renderer (rectify/visualize, panels.py, tracks.py) reads this file or its byte-identical copy rectify/visualize/rna_tokens.json (kept in sync by tests/sync_tokens.sh --check). Edit HERE, run tests/palette_check.py, then sync. Never hard-code a colour, font size or stroke weight anywhere else.
provenance: Layer A hexes are the Okabe-Ito colour-vision-deficiency-safe set (Wong, B. 'Points of view: Color blindness', Nature Methods 8, 441 (2011), doi:10.1038/nmeth.1618) exactly as Kevin approved them in Chanfreau planning/806_house_palette.py (2026-08-26), with ONE replacement (control) made after measurement -- see `meaning.control`. Layer B marks and the plum control were SEARCHED, not picked: an HLS grid of ~2,000 candidates scored with the MAGESTIC validator's CIEDE2000 + Vienot dichromat simulation against every layer-A role and every neutral under normal, deuteranopia and protanopia, filtered to contrast >= 2.0 on paper. Structural greys are 806's own ramp. Validated by tests/palette_check.py (rna-figure), which imports the maths of ~/.claude/skills/magestic-figure/tests/palette_check.py rather than forking it. Scoped by Chanfreau planning/871 (2026-09-04); decisions ruled by Kevin 2026-09-05 (two layers with a hard boundary; B neutral-first with accents disjoint from A; sample identity from A, strand by position; replace control, declare focal/stratum_a).

layers._doc: THE ONE DESIGN DECISION (871 section 3, ruled by Kevin 2026-09-05). Two colour contracts coexist in one figure and must never be confused. Layer A colours name an ARGUMENT ROLE and are applied to data panels. Layer B colours name a MOLECULAR IDENTITY and are applied to RNA glyphs. The rule that keeps them apart: LAYER B COLOURS NAME MOLECULES AND NEVER CARRY AN ARGUMENT; LAYER A COLOURS CARRY THE ARGUMENT AND ARE NEVER APPLIED TO A MOLECULAR GLYPH. A gene track under a bar chart uses B; the bars use A. This is the analogue of MAGESTIC's 'structure is never coloured'.

A.name: argument roles
A.contract: One colour = one ARGUMENT ROLE across the whole manuscript. FOCAL is never a plain category colour; if two series are strata of one measurement they take stratum_a / stratum_b and FOCAL stays free for the annotation that carries the point. REFERENCE is never used for a second focal series. Greys carry everything the argument does not turn on.
applies_to: signal glyphs coloured by SAMPLE: coverage fills, junction arcs, read pileups, 3'-end profiles
A.source: Chanfreau planning/806_house_palette.py, hexes verbatim except `control` (measured collapse, see meaning.control). Legacy aliases VERM/BLUE/GREEN/ORANGE/SKY/PURPLE/GREY map onto these roles so a script adopts with a one-line import swap.

B.name: molecular identities
B.contract: One colour = one MOLECULAR IDENTITY, forever, in every figure of both labs. Neutral-first: the gene model (exon, UTR, intron), reads and single-sample coverage are drawn in the structural greys -- structure is never coloured. Hue is spent on three MARKS only, and a B accent is a mark (tick, arc, lollipop), never a fill.

neutral_glyphs.utr: ink fill at utr_height_ratio of the exon height (form carries the distinction, not colour)
neutral_glyphs.intron: hairline stroke in `hairline` grey, optional chevrons in the direction of transcription
neutral_glyphs.tss: bent arrow in ink at the 5' end
neutral_glyphs.read: `subtle` fill for an aligned block; soft-clip = `mute` fill with hatch; junction gap = hairline
neutral_glyphs.strand: carried by POSITION (mirrored above/below the axis) and by arrow direction, never by hue (Kevin, 2026-09-05)
neutral_glyphs.read_tail: the A-rich poly(A) PREFIX of a read's 3' clip is a `polya` fill on that read -- ONE hue for the 3' end, its site mark and its tail (rbrowse paints tails base-A green on screen; the publication path keeps one identity per hue). A 1-px ink rule at the body/tail junction is the form cue (rbrowse finding [9]: that boundary is the most-read edge in the tool and a rule survives any palette)
neutral_glyphs.read_clip: the non-A remainder of a soft clip is `mute` -- unaligned, not poly(A)
neutral_glyphs.compressed_reads: a merged raster (per-column MAJORITY) or a ribbon wedge (per-column FRACTION as height) -- rbrowse's representations, ported to rectify.visualize.pileup; the body is `subtle` or the sample's layer-A role
neutral_glyphs.isoform_identity: a LETTER badge at the 3' anchor and on the isoform row, never a hue (Kevin, rbrowse 2026-08-12: 'too many colors on the figure'); shared-suffix chains are hatched

applies_to: compressed read views (merged raster, ribbon wedge)
union-exon (spliced) axis and isoform chain rows
junction arcs as counts (signal) or annotation

layers.boundary_rule: A colour from layer A never touches a molecular glyph; a colour from layer B never encodes a sample, a condition, a stratum or a claim. Enforced by API: tracks.gene_model / tracks.mark take no colour argument at all; panels.* take a ROLE name, not a hex.
layers.signal_rule: Ruled by Kevin 2026-09-05. A SIGNAL glyph (coverage fill, junction arc drawn as counts, read pileup, per-position 3'-end profile) is DATA ABOUT A SAMPLE, so when a panel compares samples its fills take layer-A roles (which sample the claim is about IS the argument). A single-sample signal is `subtle` grey. An ANNOTATION glyph (gene model, site marks, arcs drawn as annotation) is a molecule and stays in layer B. Plus/minus strand is mirrored above/below the axis in the same colour, never a hue.
layers.cross_layer_separation: MEASURED 2026-09-05: every B mark clears every A role at dE2000 >= 16.6 in normal, deuteranopia and protanopia (worst: match vs mod, deuteranopia). Five of the six A fills sit >= 17 L* LIGHTER than every B mark (A fills L* 46-71; B marks L* 23-40); the plum `control` (L* 35) is the exception and clears the marks by hue (>= 14.4) and by form instead. B marks share hue FAMILIES with A (a dark red beside vermillion, an indigo beside blue, a forest green beside green) because seven Okabe-Ito hues already occupy the hue circle; hue distance, lightness and form (mark vs fill) together are what stop a reader linking them -- DESIGN.md section 2 says why that is enough.

roles._doc: Every token has a role. The validator applies DIFFERENT rules per role.

semantic.rule: Encodes an argument role (layer A) or a molecular identity (layer B). All nine must be mutually distinguishable under normal, deuteranopia and protanopia (dE2000 >= 12) and reach contrast >= 2.0 on paper. A pair between declarable_min_delta_e and 12 may be admitted ONLY with a named form cue in `cvd_redundancy`; below declarable_min_delta_e a declaration is refused and the hex must change (that is how `control` was replaced).

structural.rule: 806's grey ramp. Carries no meaning of its own: text, spines, rails, exon fills, intron lines, single-sample signal, denominators. `neutral` is 806's NEUTRAL (#999999, 'not part of the argument') and is allowed inside a data set as the recessive series; it is checked against the accents it sits beside like any other member of a set. The grey ramp is a HIERARCHY, not a set of categories: two greys are never asked to carry independent meaning against each other, so the validator does not score structural x structural pairs -- except `neutral`, the one grey that acts as a data series, which is scored against everything it sits beside.

background.rule: The ground and 806's three tints (fills that must not compete with the line or edge in the same role: a confidence band, a floor band, a highlighted window). Being near-invisible against paper is the function, so no contrast floor applies, and nothing may ever be encoded by one of these alone.

meaning._doc: The semantic contract. Layer A: one colour = one argument role, per manuscript. Layer B: one colour = one molecular identity, forever.
meaning.focal: LAYER A. The claim this manuscript makes -- the excluded register, the observed hits, the effect being argued. Never a plain category colour.
meaning.reference: LAYER A. What FOCAL is measured against -- expectation under the null, the writer consensus, the reference rate, the control arm of a two-arm comparison.
meaning.match: LAYER A. Sequence compatibility as an argument -- a motif that DOES fit (methylatable A, DRACH-compatible, MIG). Note the boundary: a modification MARK on a transcript glyph is layer B `mod`; 'the fraction of sites that are compatible' in a bar chart is `match`.
meaning.stratum_a: LAYER A. First stratum of a split of one measurement (terminal vs interior introns; 293T vs HeLa; SMA vs control arm when neither is the claim).
meaning.stratum_b: LAYER A. Second stratum of that same split. Greyscale twin of stratum_a (dL* 0.8) -- panels.bars hatches it, which is the declared cue.
meaning.control: LAYER A. Composition / shuffle / perturbation controls. REPLACED 2026-09-05 (Kevin's ruling, option 'replace CONTROL, declare FOCAL/STRATUM_A'): 806's #CC79A7 measured dE2000 5.2 from `neutral` under deuteranopia and dL* 2.2 -- a deuteranope, and every reader of a mono printout, could not tell a control series from a denominator. #853272 was searched over hue 270-345 x saturation x lightness (1,639 survivors) for the candidate closest to the original purple that clears every A role, every B mark and every neutral at dE >= 14 in three visions with dL* >= 15 from `neutral`; worst pair is reference under protanopia at 14.4. 806_house_palette.py itself is unchanged; approved figures stay diff-able and adopt when next touched.
meaning.splice: LAYER B. The splice as a molecule: 5'SS and 3'SS ticks, the branch point dot, a junction arc drawn as ANNOTATION (an arc drawn as counts per sample is a signal glyph and takes a layer-A role). Searched: worst dE 20.2 vs reference under deuteranopia; L* 23.
meaning.polya: LAYER B. The 3' end as a molecule: the poly(A) / CPA / PAS site mark, a metaplot anchor line at the CPA. Searched: worst dE 21.5 vs ink under protanopia, 22.3 vs focal; L* 31. Drawn as a circle-headed lollipop so it separates from `splice` (dL* 7.3) and `mod` by form as well as hue.
meaning.mod: LAYER B. An RNA modification mark (m6A, pseudouridine) on a transcript glyph, drawn as a diamond-headed lollipop. Searched: worst dE 16.6 vs match under deuteranopia (the two are related concepts -- a compatible motif and the modification on it -- so a family resemblance helps rather than misleads); L* 40.
meaning.ink: 806 INK 0.15: body text on figures, exon fills, TSS arrows, rails, panel letters.
meaning.hairline: 806 HAIRLINE 0.25: bar edges, axis spines, intron lines, the zero line of a mirrored track.
meaning.subtle: 806 SUBTLE 0.45: provenance footer, secondary annotation, single-sample coverage fill, aligned-read blocks.
meaning.neutral: 806 NEUTRAL: denominators, universes, 'not part of the argument' -- the recessive data series.
meaning.mute: recessive: soft-clip blocks, dividers, 'other' categories, process arrows.
meaning.wash: 806 FLOOR_BAND 0.88: 'below this is not a measurement' shading, highlighted windows, panel wash.
meaning.focal_tint: 806 FOCAL_TINT: the band or fill under a FOCAL line (a CI ribbon), never a series on its own.
meaning.reference_tint: 806 REFERENCE_TINT: the band or fill under a REFERENCE line.
meaning.match_tint: 806 MATCH_TINT: the band or fill under a MATCH line.

cooccurrence_sets._doc: A single panel gets 2 neutrals + AT MOST 4 semantic accents. These are the sanctioned combinations, named for the panel type that uses them; the validator checks each set, not the whole vocabulary at once. Cross-layer sets (a browser view whose signal is coloured by sample) are listed explicitly so the A x B separations are validated where they actually meet.

cvd_redundancy._doc: A semantic pair that measures between roles.semantic.declarable_min_delta_e and min_delta_e under red-green CVD is admitted ONLY here, with the non-colour cue that carries the distinction named. The validator refuses a declaration below the declarable floor and refuses one without a `_cue_` note. Three states, as in greyscale_redundancy: declared (cue named), unreviewed (advisory), undeclared (FAIL).
cvd_redundancy._cue_focal_stratum_a: Okabe-Ito vermillion vs amber measures dE2000 11.8 under deuteranopia (MAGESTIC replaced its `edit` for the same pair). Kept verbatim on Kevin's ruling (2026-09-05) because 806's own rule of use already supplies the cue: when stratum fills are present FOCAL is an ANNOTATION -- the fold arrow, the outline, the called-hit marker, the text -- and never a bar fill. panels.bars refuses role='focal' beside stratum fills unless kind='annotation'.
cvd_redundancy._cue_match_neutral: Okabe-Ito green vs 806's #999999 measures dE2000 10.4 under deuteranopia. Cue: `neutral` is the recessive denominator series and panels.bars draws it with NO edge and at 0.85 alpha while `match` carries an ink edge; where both are lines, `neutral` is dashed.

greyscale_redundancy._doc: A distinction that ENCODES something must survive a mono printout. Where a sanctioned set holds a semantic pair below dL* 15, the pair is listed here ONLY if the drawing carries a non-colour cue, and the cue is named. 'unreviewed' means nobody has checked the figures that use that set -- advisory, not a pass. Measured L*: focal 54, reference 46, match 58, stratum_a 71, stratum_b 70, control 35, splice 23, polya 31, mod 40.
greyscale_redundancy._cue_stratum_a_stratum_b: dL* 0.8 -- identical in mono. panels.bars applies a hatch to every stratum_b fill (and an open marker to stratum_b points); this is code-enforced, not per-figure effort.
greyscale_redundancy._cue_focal_stratum_a: FOCAL is an annotation (arrow, outline, marker, text), never a fill, beside stratum fills (806's rule of use, code-enforced in panels.bars). An annotation against a bar is a form difference in any printout.
greyscale_redundancy._cue_focal_stratum_b: Same cue as focal/stratum_a: FOCAL is an annotation, never a fill, beside strata.
greyscale_redundancy._cue_splice_polya: Three different SHAPES by construction in tracks.mark: splice = tick with an inward triangle (or an arc), polya = circle-headed lollipop, mod = diamond-headed lollipop. A mark carries its identity by form; hue is the second channel.
greyscale_redundancy._cue_focal_reference: In a browser view tracks.coverage draws ONE sample per row, each row carrying its label, so two samples are separated by position and text, not by value. Two samples overlaid on one axes must take stratum_a / stratum_b (hatched), never focal / reference -- written into tracks.coverage's docstring.

typography._doc: Same family and floors as magestic-figure v1.1.0, so a Chanfreau figure and a MAGESTIC figure on one page share one type scale. Arial FIRST for the same measured reason (Helvetica Neue and Helvetica register at weight 400 only on this machine, so fontweight='bold' silently renders regular; Arial carries 700). 806's 7.0 pt base is BELOW the house floor: Kevin ruled three times after 806 was written (2026-09-01, 2026-09-03 x2) that the 6-9 pt scale renders too small, and the floor follows the later ruling. Nature's 5-7 pt is a MINIMUM, not a target.

conventions.panel_letter: bold lowercase a, b, c at the top-left of the axes (figure-standard owns this)
conventions.gene_names: italic for gene names in every organism (PDH1, TMEM41B); roman for proteins (Rna15, Ysh1) and for RNA species (mRNA, snRNA)
conventions.coordinates: chrXVI:558,219-560,137 with thousands separators; kb on a browser axis; 5' -> 3' left to right, so a minus-strand locus is drawn on a REVERSED x-axis
conventions.units: thin space before unit; 'nt' for RNA lengths, 'bp' for genomic, 'kb' on axes
conventions.primes: use U+2032 (′) for 5′ and 3′, never an apostrophe

typography._family_doc: Arial first for the bold-weight reason magestic-figure measured. 'DejaVu Sans' is listed as the glyph fallback, BUT MEASURED 2026-09-05 on matplotlib 3.9.4: the rcParams family list does NOT fall through per glyph -- '★ ⊘ ▮ ⇢ ✱ ∼' rendered as tofu with this list in rcParams, with or without a trailing generic. Only an EXPLICIT per-Text list -- Text(..., fontfamily=['Arial', 'DejaVu Sans']) -- engages the fallback. So any Text that carries a glyph outside Arial/Helvetica (the isoform class glyphs, the spliced ruler's ~) must set fontfamily explicitly; rectify.visualize.pileup does. figure-qa's overlap gate cannot see tofu; its glyph_coverage check can.

geometry._doc: Stroke tiers and floor as magestic-figure v1.1.0 (STROKE_SCALE 1.6 promoted to the house default on 2026-09-03). Track geometry is in fractions of the track's unit height so a gene model looks the same in a 0.4 in strip and a 1.2 in panel.
geometry._track_doc_pileup: merged_alpha_floor: a merged raster column with one read in n draws at this alpha, a full column at 1.0 (rbrowse drawMergedRow: 0.20 + 0.80 * fraction). spliced_gap_bp: the fixed width of a collapsed segment in union-exon space (rbrowse GAP_PX 20 px ~ 60 bp-units at a typical ppb). spliced_seg_cap_bp: a kept NON-exonic segment longer than this is compressed to this width and the ruler marks it (rbrowse SEG_CAP_BP). band_floor_mm: the smallest height ONE drawn cluster band may have on the page, 0.80 mm = rbrowse RIBBON_MIN_PX 4 layout px x FIG_PANEL_GAIN 1.8 at a 183 mm column -- below it a band is a hairline and reads as absent. pitch_floor_mm: the smallest per-read row pitch a squished stack may use, 0.423 mm = stroke_min_pt 0.6 drawn + 0.6 gap; at a 25.4 mm budget that is 60 reads, which is also rbrowse AUTO_DENSITY squished threshold. Chanfreau planning/880.

principles._doc: Carried over from 806 and magestic-figure; the RNA-specific ones were learned on the m6A set and the cryptic-intron set.
principles.1_two_layers: Argument roles on data panels; molecular identities on glyphs; never cross (layers.boundary_rule).
principles.2_structure_is_grey: Gene models, reads and single-sample signal are drawn in the grey ramp. Hue is spent on the three marks and on the argument.
principles.3_one_role_per_hex: A hex never changes meaning between figures of one manuscript (806's reason for existing).
principles.4_form_is_the_second_channel: Every distinction that encodes something survives a mono printout: hatch for stratum_b, shape for the three marks, annotation-not-fill for focal beside strata.
principles.5_five_to_three: A locus is read 5' -> 3' left to right; a minus-strand locus reverses the x-axis rather than mirroring the reader.
principles.6_signal_is_data: Coverage, arcs-as-counts and pileups belong to a SAMPLE and are coloured by the argument; annotation belongs to the molecule.
principles.7_rank_visual_weight: Three stroke tiers and a 2-neutral + <= 4-accent budget per panel.
